name: 2D Texture-Based Volume Rendering
definition: A GPU rendering method where volumetric data is stored in 2D texture images, projected onto the image plane as object-aligned slices, and blended back-to-front.
summary: 2D Texture-Based Volume Rendering decomposes volumetric data into axis-aligned 2D slices stored as textures, compositing them back-to-front to enable hardware-accelerated rendering on systems lacking 3D texture support.
